To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the CYP1a1 Msp1 polymorphism was associated with an increase in the risk for lung cancer in Caucasians; (2) the association was equally strong for both adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma; (3) the association was stronger in men than in woman.
Caucasians with the homozyggous variant of the CYP 1A1 gene have an increased risk of developing lung cancer, and that the risk increases with the duration of smoking.

Caucasians with the homozygo‐ us variant of the CYP 1A1 MSpI RFLP have a higher risk for lung cancer than individuals with the reference allele, and that this association is equally strong for squa‐ mous cell and adenocarcino‐ mas.

there is no clear evidence that the CYP1 A1 polymorphisms are related to the risk of lung adenocarcinoma.

there is an association between the homo­zygous variant MspI Rflp of the Cyp1A1 gene and the risk of lung can­cer in Caucasians, but not in Asian subjects, and that this association is more pronounced among smokers than in never smokers.
the CYP1 A1 Msp I polymorphism is associated with an increased risk of lung cancer in Caucasians, and the association is stronger in men than in woman.

CYP1A2 polymorphisms are not associated with lung cancer risk in a large meta‐analysis.
the association of the CYP 1A1 polymorphisms with lung cancer risk is not consistent across all studies.
